o:
We simply walk the array and add elements at even indices while subtracting elements at odd indices. With n at most 100 this is a pure simulation problem; no data structure or algorithmic trick is involved.

Example 1: 1 - 3 + 5 - 7 = -4. Example 2: a single element sits at index 0 (even), so the answer is the element itself.
k: Sign is determined purely by index parity: + for even, - for odd
A single pass with a toggling sign (or (-1)^i) suffices

a.i: Keep a running sum and flip the sign after each element. Equivalently multiply nums[i] by (-1)^i.
s: For each element, add sign * element, then negate sign
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the array
a.sp: O(1) — only an accumulator and a sign flag

w: Trivial simulation; in an interview state the parity rule and code it directly. There is no meaningful second approach. Watch for nothing in particular here — values are tiny so overflow is impossible.
